# Imajin

> You compose. Imajin orchestrates. Signed. Legible. Imajin is Agentic Relation Management.

Imajin records proof of history, not proof of work. A signature identifies an assertion's signer; it does not prove the assertion true. Actor signatures, node-witnessed actions and unsigned logs have different evidentiary strength.

## What Imajin is

The kernel serves six primitives: **Attestation · Communication · Attribution · Settlement · Discovery · Revocation**. Identity is their subject, not another primitive.

The kernel hosts shared services and rails. Apps built on Imajin register their own identities and integrate through scoped public APIs; they do not import kernel internals or share service-owned tables. Broker-agent and corpus are internal services, not independently registered vertical apps.

Imajin is source-available under the [Imajin Network License](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/LICENSE.md).

## Key concepts

- **Identity and DIDs:** People, agents and groups have distinct DIDs. Key-backed identities use Ed25519; soft identities do not have an actor signing key. Standing tiers are soft, preliminary, established, steward and operator. A tier is not blanket permission.
- **Acting identity:** A signed-in human can act as a business or organization. `x-acting-as` selects that context; the kernel still checks live membership, role and allowed services. A refused org action must not silently fall back to the personal DID.
- **Attestations:** Signed statements carry provenance. Node-witnessed records prove that the node recorded an authorized action, not that the subject signed with a device-held private key.
- **.fair and settlement:** Manifests describe attribution and payment distribution. Fees, signature requirements and settlement behavior depend on the selected flow; a manifest is not proof of payment.
- **MJN and MJNx:** MJN is receipt-backed and withdrawable subject to the rail's rules. MJNx is emitted for in-platform use and is not withdrawable. The ledger keeps them separate and does not silently convert between them.
- **Agents and delegation:** An agent has its own DID and credentials. Assignment identifies whom it serves; capability grants and live route checks determine what it may do. Human approval and scoped delegation are not interchangeable.
- **Connectors:** People connect provider accounts on their profiles. Apps invoke permitted kernel operations instead of receiving raw provider credentials. Organization keys, member consent and administrative suspension have separate authority checks.
- **Custody and revocation:** The vault supports node-sealed and delegation-grant custody. Tier 0 remains node-controlled, not zero-custody. Revocation retains signed history rather than deleting records.

## How to integrate

1. Start with the [registered-app contract](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/docs/REGISTRATION.md) and [app template](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-app-template). Register the app's identity and request only the scopes it needs.
2. Use the published [auth-client SDK](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/packages/auth-client/README.md) for sign-in. Begin login in the app, preserve callback state, and exchange the single-use authorization code with the app's signing key. Trust the kernel-returned subject, not client-supplied profile data.
3. Use a user-delegated token for consented user operations or an operator-approved app-service token for documented machine operations. Registration and operator approval do not substitute for a user's consent.
4. Fetch the relevant service spec below for request formats, auth and errors. Treat internal and development-only operations as restricted, not integration shortcuts.
5. For agents, use the agent's own credentials and the principal's explicit grants. For inference, discover the caller's usable models; an identity selector never grants access to another identity's key.
6. For connectors, keep lifecycle and custody in the kernel. Org-held keys are write-only, including for the loading admin; human members require their own active member grant, while assigned agents use their verified principal relationship.

Agent self-discovery through `GET /infer/v1/self` returns identity, usable models, inference routes, authority, grant status and fixing controls. Read-only MCP/HTTP rows reuse tool-call authorization predicates, including the authority lane and `authorizedScopes`, without probing credentials; inference scope is not tool authority. The `?agents=1` operator view backs `/jin` cards for bound serving agents.

Chat uses TLS in transit and stores plaintext at rest on the hosting node in `chat.messages_v2.content`. Push notifications carry the first 200 characters of the message preview. Message encryption is planned but not implemented; no forward-secrecy or post-compromise guarantee is made.

## Service specifications

These links correspond to the kernel's service spec definitions, not a deployment inventory or permission grant. Substitute your node's origin when integrating with another node. Specs are the route catalogue; this document is not.

- [Auth API](https://jin.imajin.ai/auth/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Calendar API](https://jin.imajin.ai/calendar/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Chat API](https://jin.imajin.ai/chat/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Cloudflare API](https://jin.imajin.ai/cloudflare/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Connections API](https://jin.imajin.ai/connections/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Github API](https://jin.imajin.ai/github/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Google API](https://jin.imajin.ai/google/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Infer API](https://jin.imajin.ai/infer/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Jin API](https://jin.imajin.ai/jin/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Media API](https://jin.imajin.ai/media/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Notify API](https://jin.imajin.ai/notify/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Pay API](https://jin.imajin.ai/pay/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Profile API](https://jin.imajin.ai/profile/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Quickbooks API](https://jin.imajin.ai/quickbooks/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Registry API](https://jin.imajin.ai/registry/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Usage API](https://jin.imajin.ai/usage/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.
- [Vault API](https://jin.imajin.ai/vault/api/spec): Authentication, schemas and operation contracts.

Corpus has its own [service-owned runbook and spec source](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/tree/main/apps/corpus). It is an internal daemon; use its configured private service address, not an assumed public kernel path.
